The Hyundai IONIQ 5 is the most popular EV in America outside of Tesla, but its larger three-row sibling looks like the better deal right now.
Hyundai IONIQ 5 vs IONIQ 9 lease comparison
Through September, the Hyundai IONIQ 5 was the third top-selling EV in the US, behind the Tesla Model Y and Model 3.
Hyundai’s electric SUV is outselling rivals like the Chevy Equinox EV, Ford Mustang Mach-E, and Toyota bZ.
Why? For one, it’s one of the most affordable EVs in the US, starting at about $35,000, and Hyundai has been offering some of the most attractive lease deals.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
After the $7,500 federal EV tax credit expired at the end of September last year, Hyundai responded by reducing prices on the IONIQ 5 by up to nearly $10,000 on some trims.
The 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 starts at $35,250. That’s for the standard-range IONIQ 5 SE with an EPA-estimated range of up to 245 miles. Upgrading to the extended-range SE RWD model adds $2,500, starting at $37,750, and offers up to 318 miles of range.
2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 (Source: Hyundai)
Hyundai’s three-row electric SUV, the IONIQ 9, starts at $58,955, or nearly $24,000 more than the base IONIQ 5 SE.
On Hyundai’s website, the 2027 IONIQ 5 SE Standard Range is available to lease from $359 a month. The offer is for a 24-month lease with $4,999 due at signing for an effective cost of $567 per month.
Hyundai IONIQ 9 at HMGMA test track (Source: Hyundai)
The extended-range Hyundai IONIQ 5 SE RWD can be leased from $369 a month. The offer is also a 24-month lease with $4,999 due at signing, for an effective cost of $577 per month.
Hyundai’s larger IONIQ 9, meanwhile, is available to lease from $419 a month. That deal also includes $4,999 due at signing, but is for a 36-month lease, so the effective cost is $557 per month.
Using Hyundai’s payment calculator , it would cost about $412 a month to lease the 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 SE for 36 months with $4,999 due at signing. With an effective cost of $550 per month, it’s only $7 less than the three-row IONIQ 9.
2026 Hyundai IONIQ 9 interior (Source: Hyundai)
The Hyundai IONIQ 9 offers more range than its smaller sibling, with an EPA-estimated range of up to 335 miles for the base SE trim.
The IONIQ 5 is a midsize electric SUV, about the same size as a Tesla Model Y, with two rows and enough room for five passengers. Hyundai’s larger IONIQ 9 offers three rows of seating and six- or seven-seat configurations.
Hyundai IONIQ 5 interior (Source: Hyundai)
With an added row of seating, the IONIQ 9 offers up to 163.54 cubic feet of interior passenger volume, compared with the IONIQ 5, which offers up to 106.5 cubic feet.
While the IONIQ 9 may be the better deal right now, the IONIQ 5 is still a good fit for those looking for a smaller, more efficient SUV that doesn’t necessarily need the added space.
2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 interior (Source: Hyundai)
In comparison, the standard Tesla Model Y RWD is listed for lease starting at $499 a month with an EPA range of up to 321 miles. That’s for a 36-month lease with $3,000 down.
Using Tesla’s payment calculator, if you put the same $4,999 down for a 24-month lease like the IONIQ 5, the Model Y RWD’s monthly rate is $549.
Which one would you choose? The IONIQ 5, IONIQ 9, or Tesla Model Y? Let us know why in the comments.
Hyundai’s electric vehicle conquest rates (Source: Peter Johnson/ Electrek/ Hyundai)
Both the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 are built at Hyundai’s Metaplant America outside of Savannah, Georgia.
Top comment by CyanPlanet
Liked by 8 people
I really haven’t seen much value in leasing. I’d rather buy the car outright using cash, with the goal of keeping the car for 10+ years.
My family recently bought a Hyundai IONIQ 5, and it is an outstanding car. Loaded with great features — both on the EV side and then for safety and comfort.
View all comments
When we toured the facility earlier this year, Hyundai told us that its electric SUVs are attracting new buyers to the brand at a higher rate than its gas or hybrid vehicles.
The IONIQ 5 had a 69.8% conquest rate last year, while the IONIQ 9 had 64.3%. Hyundai’s Elantra N ranked third (61.9%), followed by the Palisade (61.2%) and Kona Electric (60.9%).

1967 Ford Mustang Spent 20 Years in a Garage, New Owner Cries When He Sees It Cleaned Up
21 photos
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube
A car enthusiast bought a 1967 Ford Mustang. It has been his dream car for as long as he can remember. But his dream car was parked 20 years ago, and it has never moved an inch since. But he is dreaming of cruising down the road with the top down, so first things first: he has to get it cleaned up.
Under a thick layer of grime and dust, the Candy Apple Red, paint code T, has long lost its shine. The Candy Apple Red was first introduced to the Mustang palette in 1966 and offered through the early 1970s, including on 1967 models, Mach 1s, and Shelbys.
This is an original Saskatchewan car, which means it comes with deep ties to the province of Saskatchewan, located in western Canada. The new owner, Nolan, picked it up about a month ago. Now, he loads it onto his trailer and drives straight to a detailing studio. The Mustang doesn’t run and doesn’t drive, but luckily, the tires hold air, so they manage to unload it and push it straight into the studio, so that work can begin.
Ford produced a total of 472,121 Mustangs for the 1967 model year , which was not even close to the 607,568 units sold during the previous year, and this is one of them. The car was sold new in Swift Current, Saskatchewan. The original owner kept it until the 2000s, when it was sold to someone who did extensive work on it. But then, life happened, and he no longer had time for it. So he parked it and just let it sit there for years and years.
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube He sold it after 26 years of ownership and 20 years of neglect, during which it collected dust instead of miles. Back in 1967, it rolled off the production line with a 289-cubic-inch V8 under the hood, but it got replaced by a 351 Cleveland along the way. Ford never sold the Mustang with the Cleveland before 1970. The base variant came with a two-barrel carburetor and 250 horsepower.
The most powerful iteration came in 1971. The Cleveland V8 came with a four-barrel carburetor and forged internals under the hood of the Mustang Boss 351, a one-year-only homologation-style street racer of which only 1,806 examples were built. The V8 pumped out 330 horsepower.
The moment the detailer sees it, he says it needs a miracle. Mice have turned the cabin into their playground, chewing just about everything they could find, be it edible or not. Spider webs have conquered the dashboard and gauges and every territory they could find available.
An absolute disaster on wheels, this 1967 Ford Mustang will take more than just some TLC from detailer Mitch and owner Nolan to be restored to its former glory. Power washing, foaming, and rinsing remove most of the dirt it collected over two decades.
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube The car was repainted by the previous owner at some point. Now, it looks fragile, and it is flaking off, so he needs to be careful not to make it worse than it already is. However, he ends up peeling off part of the hood unintentionally during rinsing. Nolan is planning to repaint the whole car anyway, as part of an entire restoration process that has already started with this detailing procedure.
The cabin looks like a rolling trash bin. Mice have surely turned the place into their home. He finds members of the rodent family left behind. While all those in the footwell and trunk were not exactly feeling very well, as in “no longer breathing,” one of them is very much alive and kicking, playing in the labyrinth of holes in the driver’s door, which is missing the interior panel.
The vacuum cleaner and the stain extractor work miracles on the carpet, but the smell is still there. However, after all the years of neglect, the seats upholstered in black vinyl have held up surprisingly well. The grime acted like a protective layer, and Mitch’s leather cleaner reveals nearly impeccable vinyl surfaces.
In the meantime, the trunk is far worse. That is where the uninvited guests, the mice, must have spent most of the time. Mitch uses the steamer and his all-purpose cleaner to decontaminate the cabin, where every inch of every surface is filthy.
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube Polishing brings the shine back to the Candy Apple Red. Mitch uses the correcting compound to bring the shine back to the chrome bumpers and trim and turn the 1967 Ford Mustang from a nightmare to a dream.
When he steps into the studio, the owner can’t believe it is the same car he brought in the day before. He keeps looking at it and finds the transformation incredible. He can already see himself cruising in it, with the wind in his hair.
" I feel like the luckiest guy in the world right now. My heart is pumping like crazy ," he says. However, the luckiest guy in the world has to get that Cleveland V8 running.

Owner Decides To Sell His 1957 Chevy Bel Air That Has an Incredible Number on the Clock
44 photos
Photo: eBay seller jalle9209
What’s the first thing you typically think of when seeing a 1957 Bel Air ? For me, it’s the mystery of what’s hiding under the hood, as the final year of the Tri-Five era represented Chevrolet’s big foray into the V8 space.
This Bel Air is here to remind us about all of these. The car is being presented as a survivor, and while it only takes a few seconds to figure out that this isn’t necessarily accurate, it’s still a very intriguing classic car.
One of the main selling points is undoubtedly the mileage. The owner reveals that his “very clean survivor” has only 21,406 miles on the clock, and this is the original mileage. It’s almost too good to be true, especially because this car is 69 years old, meaning that it was driven for only approximately 300 miles every year.
This car has certainly spent an important part of its life inside, which kind of explains why it received several important upgrades and a transmission rebuild.
Photo: eBay seller jalle9209 There’s a good reason why I said that engines are the first thing I always think of whenever I come across a 1957 Bel Air. Chevrolet used this model year to introduce the 283 Turbo-Fire, an iconic engine for the GM brand that ended up making its way to almost every single nameplate in its portfolio.
The full-size family used the 283 as the base V8 for nearly one decade, and this made perfect sense. The 283 delivered a good balance of efficiency and performance, so many buyers who ordered a full-size Chevrolet didn’t feel the need for an upgrade under the hood.
The 283 was obtained by boring out the 265 to a higher displacement. The 283 joined the Bel Air lineup with a two-barrel configuration and a single exhaust, offering 185 horsepower in the lowest output setup.
If customers wanted more power, they could go for the Super Turbo-Fire 283, which replaced the two-barrel carburetor with a four-barrel and the single-exhaust system with a dual exhaust. The output was more impressive, as this upgraded 283 delivered 220 horsepower.
Chevrolet didn’t stop here, and another 283 version pushed the output to 245 horsepower thanks to dual four-barrel carburetors. A fuel-injected version served as the top configuration, using solid lifters to produce 283 horsepower.
Photo: eBay seller jalle9209 There’s a good reason why this 1957 Chevy Bel Air could end up catching the attention of so many people online. It’s not fitted with a two-barrel 283 but with a four-barrel setup rated at 245 horsepower. This is the most powerful non-fuel-injected 283 for the 1957 model year, and while no actual production numbers are available, it goes without saying that not many of these ended up seeing the daylight.
The owner says this is the original engine that came with the car when it rolled off the assembly line, and it is paired with a Turboglide automatic transmission that has already been rebuilt.
Otherwise, from a mechanical perspective, the car is in tip-top shape, albeit this is also the place where it steps away from that survivor promise. It boasts an upgraded stainless exhaust system, upgraded power brakes, a racing tachometer, a high-performance cooling fan, and a B&M shifter.
The cabin has also received some extra touches, so you’ll get a custom plus interior that should feel quite nice but is not original.
Photo: eBay seller jalle9209 Sure, this 1957 Chevy Bel Air is no longer original, but it’s honestly difficult to find a very good reason to step away. The mileage is something you see every day, and considering the car was born and raised in California, the rust invasion has never been a problem.
My recommendation is simple: call the seller and ask all your questions before you agree on a visual inspection. This Bel Air might be advertised as a survivor, but it has already received touches that push it away from this otherwise fantastic condition, so you need to see everything with your eyes before making an offer.
You still have enough time to do it, considering the listing will continue to be up for several more weeks - assuming the car doesn’t find a buyer in the meantime.
Photo: eBay seller jalle9209 As for the price, the original engine and the low miles are the things that make the car more expensive than many other 1957 Bel Airs.
The owner believes $40,000 is a fair price, but they also enabled the Make Offer option, just in case someone wants the car but doesn’t want to pay that much for it. 30 people have already added the vehicle to their watchlists, but it’s unclear if anyone is involved in talks regarding a possible purchase.
As for live verifications, you can find this car parked in Hinckley, Illinois, where it’s obviously tucked away to avoid any unnecessary problems that would end up altering its beautiful shape.

Photo: EVgo
EVgo has opened its first Supercharger station, and it’s in a Chicago grocery store parking lot. The site has 12 fast-charging stalls with both NACS and CCS plugs, and it’s the first of hundreds of Tesla Supercharger stalls EVgo plans to add across the US.
The 325 kW “EVgo Superchargers” are at Riverside Square & River’s Edge, at 3145 S Ashland Avenue. EVgo’s August announcement cited up to 500 kW for the Supercharger rollout.
The Chicago location features Magic Dock technology, which means both NACS and CCS vehicles can charge without an adapter. Drivers of compatible non-Tesla EVs can start a session through the Tesla app. If you drive a Tesla, the charging station shows up in the car’s navigation and Trip Planner. Other EVgo fast chargers with NACS plugs have been showing up in Tesla navigation since early September if you turn on third-party charging.
“By serving both Tesla and non-Tesla NACS drivers, we’re doubling EVgo’s addressable market and continuing to meet EV drivers where they are and where they want to charge,” said Badar Khan, EVgo CEO.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
EVgo owns the Superchargers and self-brands them, and Tesla runs and maintains them. The first sites will be at Regency Centers shopping plazas with grocery stores.
EVgo is also adding NACS plugs to its regular fast-charging network, a rollout it started in 2025. The company aims to have 500 of those stalls across the US by the end of 2026, with Supercharger stalls counted separately. Over the next two years, it plans to put at least one NACS plug at every EVgo site built in 2023 or later.

Low-Speed Braking Fault Prompts GM EV Recall, Over 67K Vehicles Affected
11 photos
Photo: Cadillac
As fate would have it, a Cadillac Lyriq that received a software update for an earlier brake system recall had struck a garage at low speed. That incident, reported internally on April 10, 2026, exposed another problem in the Detroit-based automaker's brake control software used by BEV3 models.
Per the latest NHTSA filing, the largest manufacturer among Detroit's Big Three now wants 67,380 vehicles back for a second update. As you might have already guessed by now, the problem is not mechanical. It's actually software controlling the brake system's control module, where iffy code may wrongly interpret wheel movement, compromising braking performance under specific circumstances.
The recall population includes the aforementioned Lyriq crossover, along with the Cadillac-branded Vistiq, the Celestiq ultra-luxury liftback, and the Chevrolet division's Blazer EV . All of them feature BEV3 underpinnings, a platform shared with the Honda Prologue, Acura ZDX, the China-market Buick Electra E5, the Cadillac Optiq, and the Chevrolet brand's Equinox EV.
Referred to as 26V717, this campaign is called N262570900 in General Motors lingo. General Motors reproduced the condition during internal testing. The problem occurs when the driver applies the brakes lightly while negotiating sharp low-speed turns. If the vehicle then crosses a bump such as an uneven transition at the end of a driveway, a momentary release and reapplication of the brake pedal causes the software to misinterpret wheel movement.
You can blame slip calculation for this error. Normal braking is said to return when the driver presses the no-no pedal again. Oddly specific, I know, but what did you expect from General Motors? In any case, this combination is why the problem is especially troublesome in environments that frequently involve tight steering angles and changes in elevation.
Photo: Cadillac Simply put, the module's software slip calculation was poorly coded. The garage incident mentioned earlier involved a 2024 model year Cadillac Lyriq that received apparently revised software as part of NHTSA recall 24V589. That earlier campaign makes the latest one particularly interesting.
GM initially saw a few similarities, but subsequent testing showed that the newer problem involved a different combination of circumstances associated with all-wheel-drive powertrains. The product investigation opened in August 2026, and its review identified 24 field complaints in total.
Said complaints arrived between February 2024 and June 2026, and GM is aware of 20 minor accidents. Two reports allege minor injuries. Per the Ford Motor Company's biggest rival, the second recall's fix comes in the form of software that addresses the 24V589 condition as well. In the Lyriq's case, affected vehicles were produced for model years 2023 through 2027.
All of them feature Performance All-Wheel Drive, specifically regular production option code X0E. The Blazer EV, meanwhile, is affected only in SS and PPV flavors. The other two Cadillac nameplates have different coverage, with GM highlighting 2025 through 2027 models.
Cadillac and Chevy dealers will update the brake system control module software to correct the slip calculation at no charge to affected customers. The update can also be performed over the air as long as the customers accept the applicable T&Cs. In over-the-air form, the update shouldn't take more than 20 minutes to install.

BYD’s luxury brand, Denza, calls it “the king of large 5-seater pure electric vehicles.” The new Denza N8 electric SUV will launch next week, offering an impressive CLTC driving range of over 1,000 km (621 miles), massive digital screens, and plenty of premium extras.
BYD sets Denza N8 EV launch date
After opening pre-orders for the new 5-seat luxury electric SUV last week, Li Hui, Denza’s general manager, said the results so far “have been excellent.”
According to Li, the Denza N8 is “definitely the most anticipated luxury SUV of the year.” Using BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries, the Denza N8 EV has a pure electric CLTC range of up to 1,003 km (623 miles) on a single charge.
That’s just as much as the N8 plug-in hybrid (PHEV) it’s replacing, which offered a combined CLTC range of 1,003 km (623 miles) on a full tank of gas and a full charge.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
While Li confirmed last week that the new EV variant would go on sale in November, he didn’t give a specific date.
Now, it’s official. Denza announced on its Weibo page on Friday that the launch event for the Denza N8 EV will be held on November 12, 2026.
BYD is still offering a limited-time promo that includes a 5,000 RMB credit for those who place a reservation with a 2,000 RMB ($200) deposit.
The Denza N8 measures 5,150 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,820 mm high, with a 3,075 mm wheelbase. That’s slightly longer than the Kia EV9 and Hyundai IONIQ 9.
It’s available with a single rear-wheel-drive (RWD) or a tri-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain. The RWD version uses a single motor producing either 320 kW (429 hp) or 370 kW (496 hp).
The tri-motor Denza N8 uses BYD’s e3 platform. The setup includes three electric motors: a 270 kW (362 hp) front motor and two 310 kW (416 hp) rear motors, for a combined output of 890 kW (1,193 hp).
Regulatory filings earlier this year revealed it will use either a 130.15 kWh or 105.79 kWh BYD Blade 2.0 battery, offering a CLTC range of up to 1,003 km (623 miles) and 800 km (497 miles), respectively.
BYD’s new Denza N8 and N8L CLTC driving range, battery specs, and more (Source: China MIIT)
The Denza N8 also features BYD’s latest Flash Charging technology, letting it recharge from 10% to 80% in just five minutes. It takes just nine minutes to go from 10% to 97%.
Inside, the five-seat electric SUV features a massive 30″ infotainment screen that spans nearly the entire passenger-side dashboard, plus a new 43″ (1.1 meter) panoramic head-up display (PHUD) at the bottom of the windshield.
Like most of its new luxury vehicles, the Denza N8 is loaded with BYD’s latest software and technology.
Added premium features include zero-gravity seating in all rows, a three-spoke steering wheel, wireless phone chargers, and ambient lighting.
The electric SUV is equipped with a roof-mounted LiDAR to support BYD’s God’s Eye 5.0 intelligent driving assistance system, plus its DiSus-A intelligent air suspension system.
BYD has yet to announce prices for the Denza N8 EV, but it will likely be slightly less than the N8L, an extended version that starts at 299,800 RMB ($45,000).

2026 SEMA Show • SRT Performance Joins the 2026 SEMA Show Featuring the First-Ever Jeep Wrangler Scrambler Concept
Tesla Is Pulling the Plug on the Cybertruck and the Internet Got the Party Started
62 photos
Photo: Tesla
The end of an ERROR. Not an era, but an ERROR. This is how the internet is defining the moment Tesla announced that it is winding down production of what was its first and might be its last pickup truck. Rest in peace, Cybertruck. You have been unloved, and probably, you won’t be missed.
Elon Musk officially announced that Tesla is pulling the plug on the Cybertruck , with production at Gigafactory Texas ending by mid-2027 to free up manufacturing capacity for the self-driving Cybercab robotaxi. The decision marks a swift end to one of the most polarizing experiments in modern automotive history.
Because that is exactly what the Cybertruck has been: an experiment that tricked the market with the wow factor before demand slowed down and completely collapsed. Driven onto the stage in Los Angeles in late November 2019. While Tesla promised it would be bulletproof, chief design Franz von Holzhausen, accidentally shattered two windows on the prototype during its live unveiling.
Elon Musk got up on stage to promise the Cybertruck would go into production by 2021, with a starting price of $39,900. However, the long-awaited EV started out in life as one more example of Musk overpromising and underdelivering.
Photo: Tesla It was a "baby" born after a four-year-long labour. The EV didn't go into production until the summer of 2023, with the first ten deliveries taking place at the factory later that year, on November 30. From that moment on, the market went crazy. Everyone wanted a piece of the Cybertruck. That is the effect of low production numbers.
Sellers couldn't care less about the resale ban It happened with the Cybertruck, and it is happening now with the Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X. Earlier today, autoevolution brought to you the $696,445 ZR1X, listed for sale with a $400,000 markup by a dealership in Arkansas.
While many customers waited for their turn to get their hands on a Cybertruck right off the factory floor, even more tried to snatch one on the used car market. Despite the resale clause that banned customers from reselling their trucks during the first year of ownership, the market was flooded with Cybertrucks.
But the market was also flooded with backlash and drama. A Porsche dealership in Orlando paid $244,000 to buy a Cybertruck. Days later, it relisted the EV for sale for a mind-blowing $289,999. Just keep in mind that the Foundation Series started at $99,990 for the Dual-Motor All-Wheel Drive variant and $119,990 for the tri-motor Cyberbeast.
Photo: Tesla Yet, no sign of Elon Musk’s $39,900 truck promised back in 2019. Tesla did roll out a single-motor, rear-wheel-drive Cybertruck in April 2025, but it started at $69,990. It was a short-lived glory (or make that disaster?) for the rear-wheel-drive entry-level Cybertruck. Tesla sold only 173 units and retired it in mid-September due to low demand. So much for making the Cybertruck affordable.
The beginning of the end From that moment on, it was the beginning of the end for the Cybertruck that did not even float, as Elon Musk promised at some point. In the meantime, Tesla and SpaceX sent the Roadster flying, but the Cybertruck is not even watertight, as customers complained of water intrusion in the cargo bed just as often as they complained about the huge windshield wiper failing or interior pillar trim coming off.
However, every cloud has a silver lining, and the Cybertruck came with its own. Many owners bragged about how FSD has simplified their lives, sparing them the trouble of driving the truck themselves. The power and speed were also something they have very much enjoyed.
The Cybertruck Cyberbeast arrived with supercar numbers and performance . Its tri-motor setup produces 845 horsepower (857 metric horsepower) and 864 pound-feet (1,171 Newton meters) of torque. The zero-tailpipe-emission truck flashes from zero to hero (0 to 60 mph or 0 to 97 kph) in 2.6 seconds, runs the quarter mile in 11.0 seconds, and tops out at 130 mph (209 kph).
Photo: Tesla While Elon Musk had promised a range of 500 miles (805 kilometers) from the stainless steel "fridge on wheels," the best the 123-kWh battery pack could do was 350 miles (563 kilometers) in the retired Cybertruck RWD.
The end of an era error
As Tesla announced the demise of the Cybertruck, the internet is already dancing on its grave, calling the moment "The end of an ERROR" and saying they won’t be missing it. Underneath Musk's original X announcement, top replies mocked the financial math, pointing out the massive R&D spend versus roughly 70,000 lifetime sales, while others joked about having to go back to roasting traditional pickup trucks. In the meantime, the Cybertruck once again got unwanted publicity, being called a "recycle bin."
On Instagram, users joked that Tesla still has a 500-unit stockpile of unsold vehicles "to satisfy demand, perhaps for a thousand years." While the backlash goes on and on, it turns out that not everyone hated the Cybertruck.
Some call it "the best Tesla that ever was" and praise it for the advanced tech, power, and speed. Who can blame them? Now that the Tesla Cybertruck is on its way out, the only high-performance electric trucks on the market will be the GMC Hummer EV Pickup Truck with 1,160 horsepower nd the Rivian R1T with 1,025 horsepower. Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production — Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 6, 2026

2026 SEMA Show • Ringbrothers Mesmerizes the SEMA Show Once Again, This Time With Billie, the 650-HP Pontiac GTO
Lamborghini Gallardo With Y-Shaped DRLs, Other Mods, Wants To Pass As a New Supercar - Rendering
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | a.c.g_design
We wanted to say that it’s been a while since the Lamborghini Gallardo ended up in our news feed, but it hasn’t, because we keep dedicating stories to this model quite constantly, and you can understand why, can’t you?
If you said no, you may want to throw away that petrolhead license, because you clearly do not need it. After all, we are talking about an exciting machine that was available with a stick shift, and had a screaming V10 behind the passenger compartment. The natural aspirated engine had a 5.0-liter displacement in pre-facelifted configuration, and was replaced with a 5.2-liter one for the mid-cycle refresh. Besides the six-speed manual transmission, it was also offered with a six-speed automated manual unit.
The Lamborghini Gallardo may be quite old, as production spanned between 2003 and 2013, with over 14,000 units estimated to have seen the light of day in total, but it remains a great driver’s car, not to mention that it still turns heads wherever it goes. Buying one of these means spending from just under $100K to almost $200K for the basic models, with manual ones commanding over $200K easily and sometimes close to $500K if we are talking about certain limited editions with only a few miles under their belts.
Needless to say that the Lamborghini Gallardo needs no aftermarket makeover in order to become more appealing. However, certain gearheads would agree to disagree, and we can understand why, because if everyone wanted their Gallardo stock, then certain tuners would find themselves struggling financially. This story is not about the tuning world, but the rendering one, because the supercar you see in the gallery is not real. It is a permanent resident of Fantasy Land, and has @a.c.g_design on Instagram behind it.
Photo: Instagram | a.c.g_design This machine definitely stands out, and has the ability to confuse people. That’s because while it retains its original design, it has been slightly modernized. For instance, those Y-spoke daytime running lights were inspired by the Revuelto, which is Lamborghini’s modern-day flagship supercar. It replaced the Aventador in the Raging Bull’s portfolio, and is more than three years old. The Revuelto has been joined by the Revuelto SV recently, and this is a rarer model with more advanced features, and extra oomph.
We can also see that the headlights are new, and they have gone down the LED route. The front hood is also new, and so are the front bumper, splitter, and other elements. The side skirts are sharper than the OEM ones, the rear wing is bigger, and the diffuser a lot larger. The taillights seem to have been inspired by those of the Temerario, aka Lambo’s new “baby” supercar, and there are extra brake lights on deck, too, as well as three exhaust tips.
The supercar in question features a dark blue paint finish on the outside, some black elements here and there, and a set of aftermarket wheels. The concave alloys have a Y-spoke pattern, and we can see the yellow brake lights behind them. The Italian flag decorates certain parts of the rendered machine, and the Superleggera name on the lower parts of the doors reveals the initial configuration of this ride.
Photo: Instagram | a.c.g_design This model had 523 horsepower (530 ps/390 kW) to play with when it was new, with the peak output available at a screaming 8,000 rpm. The Superleggera Edizione Tecnica came with 562 hp (570 ps/419 kW) on tap, and required just 3.8 seconds to sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph). Sure, that may not sound impressive by today’s standards, but between us, it is more than enough for such a thing. And let’s not forget that the Gallardo was developed in the early 2000s, and hit the assembly line back in 2003.
On top of that, it definitely acts more like a Lambo than its successors, the Huracan and the modern-day Temerario, and those who have had the chance to sit behind the wheel and take it out for a spin know what we are talking about. And in the end, the Gallardo may not be really suitable for daily drives, but it remains a very engaging machine, capable of injecting its occupants with a lot of adrenaline every time the driver abuses the loud pedal. Not to mention that it has aged like fine wine, hasn’t it?
Speaking of the design, I very much like the way the Lamborghini Gallardo looks today, and in my opinion, it is best had bone stock. What I am trying to say is while I can understand why some enthusiasts would like the way this virtually-tuned example looks, it is definitely not my cup of tea. But is it yours? Feel free to speak your mind about it in the comments section below, as it is definitely not something that you come across everyday. source_document.body:
Apollo has spent the last several years carving out a spot for itself toward the more premium end of the electric scooter market. Now the company is trying something different: going after the mass market with its least expensive model yet.
The new Apollo Dash carries a $699 MSRP, but is launching at $599 as part of the company’s Black Friday sale running through November 30. More importantly, Apollo says the Dash isn’t intended to simply be a stripped-down budget scooter, but rather a way to bring much of its existing technology down to a lower price point.
The scooter uses a 48V electrical system powering a 600W nominal, 1,200W peak-rated Bosch motor, with a top speed of 20 mph (32 km/h). Its 480Wh battery is rated for up to 25 miles (40 km) of range in Eco mode.
Apollo also claims the 48V architecture avoids limiting motor power to anemic levels as the battery drains, meaning riders shouldn’t experience the same increasingly sluggish performance toward the bottom of the battery that can occur on some lower-cost scooters.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
At 43 lb (19.5 kg), the Dash is reasonably portable, though getting the weight and price down comes with an important compromise: there’s no suspension. Apollo also caps rider weight at 220 lb (100 kg), and points heavier riders or those regularly tackling rough roads and hills toward the more expensive Apollo Go instead.
Despite the lower price, there’s still a surprisingly long feature list. The Dash gets IP66 water resistance, self-healing tubeless tires, regenerative braking, built-in turn signals, Apollo’s Beam stem light, NFC unlocking, Apple Find My integration, and connectivity with the Apollo smartphone app.
Apollo says it put the frame through 10,000 km (6,200 miles) of durability validation before shipping production units. A beta test program also accumulated 1,002 miles over 144 rides without any reported punctures or maintenance issues. Beta riders averaged 19 miles (30 km) per ride while finishing with 29% battery remaining, according to Apollo.
Perhaps the bigger story here, though, is where Apollo is positioning the Dash. The company says 52% of its customers previously owned scooters from brands including Segway, NIU, and Xiaomi, but historically moving up to an Apollo often meant crossing the $1,000 mark.
At $599 , the Dash appears designed to get those riders into Apollo’s ecosystem much earlier – while also putting the company squarely into competition with the mass-market scooters it previously sat above.
And for those wanting a bit more power or features, Apollo’s more upmarket models are on sale now as part of early Black Friday promotions .

2026 SEMA Show • Nissan Seeks Adventures at 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas With Frontier, Pathfinder, Armada Concepts
2028 Ford Ranger Gets the Mid-Cycle Refresh Procedure Inside and Outside, Though Only Virtually
19 photos
Photo: AutoYa / YouTube
The situation is pretty stable across the traditional mid-size pickup truck sector in America, with the fourth-generation N400 Toyota Tacoma leading the pack and year-to-date sales up by five percent to no less than 215k deliveries over a nine-month period.
There’s no race in the segment – the Chevrolet Colorado is 142k trucks behind Toyota, but second place is highly disputed with the Nissan Frontier, which jumped almost 40% year-to-date to hold third place just a few trucks behind the Chevy. Ford, on the other hand, sold 51,530 units so far this year of the Ranger, up about seven percent.
The company has made changes to the 2027 Bronco and Ranger, which are cousins in the SUV and mid-size pickup truck category, both losing the 2.7-liter EcoBoost V6 and the latter gaining a de-tuned 3.0L EcoBoost V6 variant for a bigger punch off the line. However, some folks aren’t satisfied with just that.
No worries, as the rumor mill, together with the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI, believes that good things are coming for the Ford Ranger – perhaps kicking off with a mid-cycle refresh procedure for the 2028 model year. Indeed, the second-generation T6-based Ranger, the fifth by its name in North America, has been around since the 2024 model year in the United States.
That means it’s perhaps the ripe time to think about a facelift for the next model year, and the good folks over at the " AutoYa " info channel on YouTube have unofficially imagined the CGI look of the refreshed 2028 Ford Ranger mid-size pickup truck with help from their resident virtual artist.
More precisely, the channel’s host thinks that next year we’ll get to see the mid-cycle refresh of the fifth-gen Ford Ranger with exterior redesigns and subtle interior changes. They also “hope” for a new plug-in hybrid powertrain to become available in North America, though we shouldn’t count on a full EV model too. More importantly, the resident pixel master has spent some time illustrating the potential changes, and we get to see them in the unofficial, hypothetical design project featured below.
The biggest changes could arrive at the front, where the CGI expert has envisioned a more muscular hood, new squarer LED headlights with the same C-shaped daytime running light signature, a larger radiator grille, and a redesigned bumper with LED fog lights. The interior, meanwhile, could gain subtler changes, like a larger central display and fresh colors.
Speaking of hues, there are also a ton of ritzy shades offered in this video, both inside and outside. So, what do you think – yay or nay? Should Ford consider a mid-cycle refresh for the Ranger, or are they too busy with the all-new Fathom affordable EV pickup truck and don’t have time for the traditional body-on-frame mid-size nameplate?

Networking
Cisco Catalyst C1300-24XTS Front 1
Today we are looking at the Cisco Catalyst C1300-24XTS. This is an interesting switch because it offers 24 independent 10GbE ports, split evenly between 12x 10Gbase-T ports and 12x SFP+ cages. That port mix matters for administrators who have a blend of 10GBase-T-capable servers or workstations alongside fiber-connected storage or uplinks. We have looked at a number of these switches before, including the C1300-16XTS , C1300-12XS , C1300-12XT-2X , and C1300-8FP-2G . The 24-port model is the one that is really neat, and it has been running without issue for months, so it is finally time for the review. Let us get into the hardware.
Cisco Catalyst C1300-24XTS Hardware Overview
The Cisco Catalyst C1300-24XTS is a 1U rackmount switch with a metal chassis. The unit measures 444.3mm by 273mm by 43.94mm and weighs 4.2kg. Unlike many of the lower-port-count models we have reviewed, this is a full 1U unit that fills out the rack and is much wider than the other units we have tested.
Cisco Catalyst C1300-24XTS Front 1
On the left side of the front panel is a cluster of management interfaces. These include several ways to access a console interface. Cisco makes this very easy.
Cisco Catalyst C1300-24XTS USB C Port 1
The twelve copper data ports are numbered 1 through 12 and support 10GBase-T. These are arranged in two rows of six on the front panel. A question we often see about switches with SFP+ and 10Gbase-T is whether they are combo jacks, these are not.
Cisco Catalyst C1300-24XTS 10 GbE RJ45 Ports 1
Next to those are twelve SFP+ cages numbered 13 through 24, arranged in three banks of four. These provide fiber connectivity options for uplinks or storage networks. Also by going with this spread-out solution, Cisco makes putting SFP+ optics and DACs into the switch easier, and cooling is a bit easier as well.
Cisco Catalyst C1300-24XTS 10 GbE SFP+ Ports 1
On the far right of the front panel, there is a dedicated RJ45 connector that operates at 1GE. This port is physically separate from both the left console connector and the 24 data ports. It provides out-of-band management access, allowing administrators to reach the switch independently of the main data plane.
Cisco Catalyst C1300-24XTS Management Port
Both rack ears came supplied with this unit and are a bit different than we saw on the 12 and 16-port models.
Cisco Catalyst C1300-24XTS Rack Ears 2
On the sides of the chassis, we get large perforated vent banks along with screws and mounting positions. Both sides are vented on this switch.
Cisco Catalyst C1300-24XTS Side 1
Moving to the rear, there is a vent, the product label, lock points or slots for securing the unit, and a single AC power input. There is no redundant power input here, so for A+B power delivery, you would need an external automatic transfer switching PDU.
Cisco Catalyst C1300-24XTS Rear 1
Next, let us get inside the switch to see what Cisco did there.
